title: Peak concurrent calls
statement:
Table calls(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, server TEXT, start_sec INTEGER, end_sec INTEGER), with start_sec < end_sec. A call is active from start_sec (included) to end_sec (excluded), so a call ending at t and another starting at t are never active together.

For each server, return the server, its peak (the largest number of its calls active at the same instant) and first_at, the earliest instant at which that peak is reached. Sort by peak, highest first, then by server.

Output: columns server, peak, first_at.
Constraints: up to 20000 calls, times from 0 to 100000. Comparing every pair of calls is too slow for the largest tests.

Example
calls:
  (1, 'eu', 0, 10)
  (2, 'eu', 5, 15)
  (3, 'eu', 10, 20)
  (4, 'eu', 12, 14)
  (5, 'us', 0, 5)
  (6, 'us', 5, 10)
Output:
eu|3|12
us|1|0

(At 10, call 1 has ended when call 3 starts, so only 2 calls are active; at 12, calls 2, 3 and 4 are.)

scenarios.name: Example
scenarios.input:
CREATE TABLE calls (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, server TEXT, start_sec INTEGER, end_sec INTEGER);
INSERT INTO calls (id, server, start_sec, end_sec) VALUES
  (1, 'eu', 0, 10),
  (2, 'eu', 5, 15),
  (3, 'eu', 10, 20),
  (4, 'eu', 12, 14),
  (5, 'us', 0, 5),
  (6, 'us', 5, 10);
